methods.label: Keep the common factors
methods.explanation:
Substituting \(r-1\) into the formula gives
\[
f(r-1)=\frac13(r-1)r(r+1).
\]
The expressions for \(f(r)\) and \(f(r-1)\) share the factors \(r\) and \(r+1\). Factoring them out avoids expanding the cubic products:
\[
\begin{aligned}
f(r)-f(r-1)
&=\frac{r(r+1)}3\bigl[(r+2)-(r-1)\bigr]\\
&=\frac{r(r+1)}3\cdot3\\
&=r(r+1).
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus the answer is \(r(r+1)\), choice A.
